metadata.title: Trusted Integration

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for evaluating and asserting aggregate trust posture for system-to-system integrations based on multiple contributing signals.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Integration control planes, trust evaluators, policy engines, and signal aggregation mechanisms.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Bridge pattern aggregating multiple integration trust signals into bounded, revocable assertions without granting implicit authority.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines trusted integration state as derived signal data, not a static credential or entitlement.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Controls governing trust evaluation, authorization decisions, and risk assessment (AC, IA, RA families).

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Zero Trust guidance stating that trust must be continuously evaluated and never implicitly granted.

metadata.remarks: Trusted Integration aggregates trust-related signals from multiple integration patterns to produce a bounded, revocable trust assertion. This pattern does not grant authorization, approve business actions, or override downstream policy or governance.

components.title: Integration Trust Aggregation
components.description: Aggregation of multiple integration trust signals into a single evaluative posture.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Multiple risk and trust indicators inform security decisions.

components.title: Integration Trust Assertion
components.description: Emission of a bounded trust assertion consumable by relying systems.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Trust assertions are generated using protected mechanisms.

components.title: Trust Revocation Signaling
components.description: Identification and signaling of conditions under which integration trust must be degraded or revoked.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Trust assertions may be withdrawn based on changing conditions.

components.title: Trusted Integration Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what a trusted integration assertion does not grant or imply.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Trusted integration status does not imply authorization, correctness, or approval of downstream actions.
